newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan State Oil up 7.78 percent.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan State Oil up 7.78 percent.

text.p: Blue chip Pakistan State Oil (PSO) jumped 27 rupees, or 7.78 percent, to 374 on Monday after the company announced favourable annual results, dealers said.
A total 9,600 PSO shares had traded hands by mid-session.

Taurus Securities said in a review that keeping in line with its tradition of high payouts, PSO announced a 30 percent cash and 30 percent bonus dividend. The company had already announced an interim dividend of 30 percent.
"The market has responded positively to the PSO results and ended the speculations about the fall in its earnings," dealer Ambreen Shoukat of KASB & Co said.
"The stock has a strong growth potential and low risk of a downside," the review by Taurus Securities said.
Dealers said the recent 7.86 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar and a 10 percent rise in petroleum prices would boost company profits.
PSO, Pakistan's largest oil company, has a market share of almost 75 percent in most petroleum products.
